title: SKM threatens to gherao Saini’s residence on December 2 over sugarcane prices

ai.summary: Farmers in Haryana demand the state government set sugarcane price at ₹600 per quintal, threatening a statewide agitation including a gherao of chief minister's residence on December 2 if their demand is not met.

facts.claim: Farmers demand minimum SAP of ₹600 per quintal
facts.quote: Farmers demand minimum SAP of ₹600 per quintal; announce seven mahapanchayats across state before November 26 as part of agitation

facts.claim: The SKM warned of a major statewide agitation, including a gherao of chief minister Nayab Singh Saini’s residence in Kurukshetra on December 2
facts.quote: The Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) on Thursday demanded that the Haryana government fix the sugarcane price at ₹600 per quintal and warned of a major statewide agitation, including a gherao of chief minister Nayab Singh Saini’s residence in Kurukshetra on December 2, if the demand was not accepted.

facts.claim: The previous sugarcane price in Haryana was ₹415 per quintal
facts.quote: The previous sugarcane price in Haryana was ₹415 per quintal.

facts.claim: The state government has increased it to ₹430 per quintal for the 2026-27 crushing season and announced a further hike to ₹450 per quintal for 2027-28
facts.quote: The state government has increased it to ₹430 per quintal for the 2026-27 crushing season and announced a further hike to ₹450 per quintal for 2027-28.

facts.claim: This amounts to a cumulative increase of just ₹35 over two years
facts.quote: This amounts to a cumulative increase of just ₹35 over two years.

facts.claim: As part of the agitation, the SKM has announced seven mahapanchayats across Haryana before November 26
facts.quote: As part of the agitation, the SKM has announced seven mahapanchayats across Haryana before November 26, followed by another round of seven such gatherings in the next phase.

ai.background_note: Farmers in Haryana are protesting over sugarcane prices, demanding ₹600 per quintal after the state government increased prices from ₹415 to ₹450 over two years, which they argue is insufficient given rising costs.
